title: Insulin Pump Program Statement of Patient Financial Responsibility
content:
### When the customer can be made responsible

When an item or quantity the customer wants on an Insulin Pump Program is expected not to be paid by the payer — above the tier's allowance without supporting documentation, an item the tier does not cover, or a replacement before the payer's replacement interval — Larkfield supplies it billable to the customer only after the customer signs the tier's advance notice of financial liability for that item and quantity before the ship date; the customer signs it personally, and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them. *The words "the customer signs it personally" are no longer in force as the signing rule for a cartridge or reservoir liability notice, whose signing follows its own current notice rule; every other liability notice remains under them, and for every notice no Larkfield representative can sign it for them.*

### The notice on each kind of tier

- **Original Medicare tier.** The notice is the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (form CMS-R-131); the claim is still submitted to Medicare with the notice on file, and the customer becomes liable only for a line Medicare denies.
- **Medicare Advantage tier.** No notice can make the member liable; the member becomes liable only for an item for which the plan has issued a pre-service organization determination denial, recorded as a prior authorization denial for that item.
- **Self-pay tier.** No notice applies, because every item is priced at the Larkfield cash price.
- **Commercial HMO, Commercial PPO and Medicaid tiers.** The notice is the tier's own form: the plan member waiver on the Commercial HMO and Commercial PPO tiers, and the Medicaid non-covered service agreement on the Medicaid tier.

### The only patient charge types

A patient charge is posted only as one of these charge types:

| Charge type | What it is |
|---|---|
| Self-pay price | a self-pay refill at the cash price |
| Standard shipping | a self-pay shipment below the free-shipping threshold |
| Expedited shipping | a customer-requested expedite |
| Non-covered item | an item or quantity covered by a signed liability notice, or by a Medicare Advantage organization determination denial, that the payer denied, charged at the Larkfield cash price of the units concerned |

*The cash-price measure in the non-covered item row is no longer in force for a non-covered item charge posted for the line the program's newest CO-151 denial bills, nor for a non-covered item charge under review for a billing correction; each of those follows its current charge rule, and every other non-covered item charge remains at the cash price.*

### Evidence a non-covered item charge requires

A non-covered item charge requires a liability notice signed on or before the ship date covering that item and at least those units, or on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan's organization determination denial for that item; without it the amount is Larkfield's write-off and is never billed to the customer.

| Hypothetical line (payer denied 10 units) | Non-covered item charge permitted |
|---|---|
| Notice for the item, 10 units, signed the day before the ship date | Yes |
| Notice for the item, 10 units, signed on the ship date | Yes |
| Notice for the item, 6 units only | Not for all 10 units — the notice must cover at least the units charged |
| Notice signed after the ship date | No — Larkfield's write-off |
| Medicare Advantage tier, plan organization determination denial for the item on file | Yes |
